clinician.final_diagnosis: Abdominal tuberculosis with M. tuberculosis identified by PCR in mesenteric lymph node biopsies
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 37-year-old Bangladeshi female housekeeper presented in September 2022 with 2 months of right-sided abdominal pain, postprandial worsening, diarrhea, bloating, and 5 kg weight loss. Physical examination revealed abdominal distension with palpable bowel loops and increased bowel sounds. CT abdomen/pelvis showed distended small bowel loops, minimal free fluid adjacent to the terminal ileum, and inflammatory changes in the caecum/ascending colon with mucosal enhancement suspicious for inflammatory bowel disease. Colonoscopy revealed a patulous ileocecal valve with terminal ileum ulcerations, ileal stenosis, and deformation of the cecum/ileocecal valves (differential included tuberculosis, Crohn's disease, or malignancy). Mesenteric lymph node biopsies were obtained, and PCR analysis identified M. tuberculosis. Laboratory evaluation showed elevated ESR. The patient was initiated on antituberculous therapy with significant clinical improvement, weight gain, and symptom resolution during outpatient follow-up.

Colonoscopy revealed patulous ileocecal valve, terminal ileum ulcerations, ileal stenosis, and deformed cecum/ileocecal valves consistent with tuberculosis, Crohn's disease, or malignancy
